fertilizer.nutrient_principles: Focus on Nitrogen for maximum tiller production and Phosphorus for strong root and shoot development. Zinc is critical in submerged conditions.
fertilizer.timing_guidance: Apply first top dressing at 20-25 DAT, second at 40-45 DAT if required
fertilizer.notes: Zinc deficiency is common in submerged rice. Apply zinc sulfate at 25 kg/ha or 0.5% foliar spray if deficiency observed.
fertilizer.risk_if_skipped: Reduced tillering, weak canopy, and poor yield potential
fertilizer.soil_type_adjustment: For light-textured sandy soils, split nitrogen into 3-4 doses; for heavy clay soils, 2-3 splits are adequate.
fertilizer.deficiency_symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaves (N), reduced tillering, stunted height, purple tinge on older leaves (P), leaf bronzing (Zn)
fertilizer.avoid_overuse: Avoid applying all nitrogen as basal. Excessive vegetative growth from over-fertilization increases lodging and disease risk.
fertilizer.weather_precautions: Apply fertilizer when soil is moist and no heavy rain is expected. Avoid application during continuous overcast or waterlogged conditions.
fertilizer.recommended_focus: Nitrogen and phosphorus support for maximum tiller production and canopy development
fertilizer.organic_alternatives: Green manuring with dhaincha or sunn hemp incorporated before transplanting. Apply well-decomposed compost at 10-15 tons/ha.
fertilizer.cost_efficiency_tip: Use leaf color chart (LCC) for need-based nitrogen application to reduce costs by 20-25% while maintaining yield.

fertilizer.nutrient_principles: Focus on Nitrogen for maximum tiller production and Phosphorus for strong root and shoot development. Zinc is critical in submerged conditions.
fertilizer.timing_guidance: Apply first top dressing at 20-25 DAT, second at 40-45 DAT if required
fertilizer.notes: Zinc deficiency is common in submerged rice. Apply zinc sulfate at 25 kg/ha or 0.5% foliar spray if deficiency observed.
fertilizer.risk_if_skipped: Reduced tillering, weak canopy, and poor yield potential
fertilizer.soil_type_adjustment: For light-textured sandy soils, split nitrogen into 3-4 doses; for heavy clay soils, 2-3 splits are adequate.
fertilizer.deficiency_symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaves (N), reduced tillering, stunted height, purple tinge on older leaves (P), leaf bronzing (Zn)
fertilizer.avoid_overuse: Avoid applying all nitrogen as basal. Excessive vegetative growth from over-fertilization increases lodging and disease risk.
fertilizer.weather_precautions: Apply fertilizer when soil is moist and no heavy rain is expected. Avoid application during continuous overcast or waterlogged conditions.
fertilizer.recommended_focus: Nitrogen and phosphorus support for maximum tiller production and canopy development
fertilizer.organic_alternatives: Green manuring with dhaincha or sunn hemp incorporated before transplanting. Apply well-decomposed compost at 10-15 tons/ha.
fertilizer.cost_efficiency_tip: Use leaf color chart (LCC) for need-based nitrogen application to reduce costs by 20-25% while maintaining yield.

water_management.critical_condition: Avoid prolonged dry periods that reduce tillering
water_management.soil_moisture: Keep soil saturated with 2-5 cm standing water

water_management.recovery_guidance: Restore standing water promptly; if stress prolonged, apply light nitrogen to recover tiller production

symptoms: Yellow to white lesions with wavy margins

prevention: Avoid field flooding that spreads bacteria

fertilizer.nutrient_principles: Focus on Potassium for grain filling and stress tolerance. Limited Nitrogen for panicle development. Boron and Zinc for pollen viability.
fertilizer.timing_guidance: Apply potassium at panicle initiation (45-50 DAT). Additional maintenance dose at early flowering if potassium deficiency is observed.
fertilizer.notes: Potassium deficiency during flowering severely impacts grain filling and quality. Foliar potassium (2% KNO3) can be applied if deficiency symptoms appear.
fertilizer.risk_if_skipped: Poor pollination, reduced grain setting, and significant yield loss
fertilizer.application_method: Split application with adequate soil moisture
fertilizer.soil_type_adjustment: On sandy/light soils, split potassium into 2 doses; on clay soils, a single dose at panicle initiation is sufficient.
fertilizer.deficiency_symptoms: Yellowing and drying of older leaf tips and margins (K), weak stems, poor panicle emergence, increased chaffy grains, lodging susceptibility
fertilizer.avoid_overuse: Avoid excess nitrogen during flowering as it increases blast disease severity and lodging risk. Avoid foliar sprays during peak heat hours.
fertilizer.weather_precautions: Do not apply fertilizer if heavy rain or storm is forecast. Avoid foliar application during high temperature (>35°C) or windy conditions.
fertilizer.recommended_focus: Potassium nutrition for grain development, stress resilience, and improved grain quality
fertilizer.organic_alternatives: Apply potassium-rich organic sources like wood ash (10-15 kg/ha) or banana pseudostem compost. Foliar spray of vermiwash or seaweed extract for micronutrients.
fertilizer.cost_efficiency_tip: Apply potassium based on soil test results to avoid over-application. Muriate of potash (MOP) is cost-effective and readily available.
